clue.text: Backward learners make mistakes

indicators.note: backward tells the solver to read the word for learners from end to start

parts.note: pupils are learners at school

explanation.surface: Pupils who are slow at school keep getting things wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backward' looks like a description of slow learners, but it tells you to turn PUPILS round.
explanation.definitionFit: To slip up is an idiom for erring or blundering.

clue.text: Son of bread that's set out with room to rise

parts.note: to set out is to depart, to leave

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the word for room is read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: a den is a small private room

explanation.surface: A loaf that has been put out with space to rise as it proves.
explanation.walkthrough: The rising dough of the surface hides the reversal: 'to rise' in a down clue means read the room word upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Leavened bread is made with yeast or another raising agent, as opposed to flat unleavened bread.

clue.text: Stone one? Not so cruel

parts.note: a pit is the stone of a fruit such as a cherry
I is the Roman numeral for one
less means not so much

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a stone is unkind, and is told it is not.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone without pity is merciless, harsh and unfeeling.

clue.text: Fish that is removed from pie, or blackbird

annotationWithheld.why: Fish that is removed from pie, or blackbird (9): PORBEAGLE reads as PIE OR BEAGLE less IE, but no clue word gives BEAGLE; 'blackbird' cannot supply it as printed and no source confirms the intended text.
annotationWithheld.clue: Fish that is removed from pie, or blackbird

clue.text: Send a girl off without name? Here's a possible one

indicators.note: off says the letters of the phrase are jumbled, and without says the letter for name is to be taken away from them

explanation.surface: Dispatch a young woman with no name, and here is one she might take.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of SEND A GIRL, minus the N for 'name', rearrange to give the girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Griselda is a female forename, a byword for the patient wife of medieval tale.

clue.text: Easy work Waugh produced for royal guards

parts.note: gentle means easy, mild, not strenuous
Men at Arms is a 1952 novel by Evelyn Waugh, the first of his Sword of Honour trilogy

explanation.surface: An undemanding book written by Evelyn Waugh, done for the palace guard.
explanation.walkthrough: Evelyn Waugh was an English novelist; Men at Arms is one of his wartime novels.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gentlemen at Arms are the British sovereign's ceremonial bodyguard.

clue.text: Clerical garb thar's sensible clothing abroad

indicators.note: clothing means the word for sensible wraps round the word for abroad

parts.note: sane means sensible, rational
out means away from home, abroad

explanation.surface: Priestly dress is the practical thing to wear when travelling overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: A soutane is a cassock, the long robe worn by Roman Catholic priests.

clue.text: True sound of the seaside

indicators.note: sound of says the word for true is heard spoken rather than written

parts.note: literal means true to the facts, exact

explanation.surface: The genuine noise of the coast: waves and gulls.
explanation.definitionFit: Littoral is an adjective for the shore, relating to the coastal strip by the sea.

clue.text: Look to take off here?

parts.note: an air is a look or appearance
to strip is to take off clothes

explanation.surface: Somewhere to look if you want a plane to leave the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: a place where aircraft take off.
explanation.definitionFit: An airstrip is a basic runway from which planes depart and land.

clue.text: Strong players giving leadership to club

indicators.note: giving leadership to means the players' word goes in front of the club's word

parts.note: the cast is the set of actors in a play
an iron is a golf club

explanation.surface: Powerful performers who give the club a lead.
explanation.definitionFit: Cast-iron means tough, unbreakable, as in a cast-iron guarantee.

clue.text: Customer takes foreign money with hesitation

parts.note: the punt was the Irish pound, a currency foreign to British readers
er is the sound of a hesitation

explanation.surface: A shopper hesitantly accepts payment in an overseas currency.
explanation.walkthrough: PUNT was the currency of the Irish Republic before the euro.
explanation.definitionFit: Punter is British slang for a client or paying patron.

clue.text: Confusion as Prime Minister introduces measure later repeated

indicators.note: introduces means the measure is brought inside the abbreviation for Prime Minister

parts.note: an ell is an old measure of cloth length
the same measure ELL, which the clue says is later repeated

explanation.surface: Muddle as the head of government brings in a policy that is later done over again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'later repeated' tells you to add a second ELL after PELLM.
explanation.definitionFit: Pell-mell means a disorderly rush, chaos and disarray.

clue.text: Unconventional escape route

explanation.surface: An unusual way of getting out.
explanation.definitionFit: Way-out is slang for weird or offbeat; a way out is an exit or means of escape.

clue.text: Make long story longer for tribal leader

parts.note: a saga is a long story
more means additional, longer

explanation.surface: A chief asks for a lengthy tale to be drawn out further.
explanation.definitionFit: A sagamore is a chief among some Native American peoples of New England.

clue.text: One who withdraws with some soldiers on vehicle

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the soldiers sit above the vehicle

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army
a tractor is a farm vehicle

explanation.surface: Someone retreating with a few troops on a farm vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: Retractor is a noun for someone who takes back a statement, recanting it.

clue.text: Combines aid with deals, being extremely selective

indicators.note: extremely means only the extreme letters, first and last, of each word are used

explanation.surface: Merges assistance with business deals, while being very picky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being extremely selective' says take only the first and last letters of 'aid' and 'deals'.
explanation.definitionFit: To add is to join one thing to another, putting them together.

clue.text: A game fighter with a composed defence

parts.note: polo is a game played on horseback
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A sporting combatant with a calm way of defending himself.
explanation.definitionFit: An apologia is a formal written justification of one's opinions or conduct.

clue.text: Terribly poor, with study unfinished, does this?

definitions.text: Terribly poor, with study unfinished, does this?

indicators.note: terribly signals that the letters which follow are thrown into disorder
unfinished means the final letter of the word study is cut off

explanation.surface: A struggling student who never completes his course: is this what he does?
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' cuts STUDY to STUD; 'Terribly' shuffles POOR with STUD.
explanation.definitionFit: To drop out is to abandon a course of education before completing it.

clue.text: Fly, for example, in part of aircraft attacked to wing

definitions.text: part of aircraft attacked to wing

explanation.surface: An insect lands on a part of a plane joined to its wing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fly' is not the insect but the opening on trousers, covered by a fold of cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: A trouser fly is a covering fold of fabric; an aircraft's hinged wing surface for lift is also so named.

clue.text: Without constraint, sack or pillage

parts.note: free means without constraint
to boot is to sack or dismiss

explanation.surface: Unrestrained, an army may sack a town or loot it.
explanation.definitionFit: To freeboot is to act as a pirate or plunderer, raiding for spoils.

clue.text: A couple of pages fail to be clear

parts.note: pp is the abbreviation for pages, plural
aren't means are not, failing to be

explanation.surface: Two sheets of a document are not legible.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparent means obvious, plainly visible.

clue.text: Broadcast listener located in Ireland

indicators.note: broadcast is scattered, so the letters of the word listener are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: A radio listener who lives in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' fits a radio surface, but it is the anagram signal; the definition describes a place on the island.
explanation.definitionFit: Leinster is one of the four historic provinces of Ireland, in the east, including Dublin.

clue.text: Briefly visits, making appearance at home

parts.note: looks means appearance
in means at home

explanation.surface: Pops round briefly, turning up at the house.
explanation.definitionFit: Looks in is a phrasal verb for making a short call on someone.

clue.text: Computer that's trim, suitable to be carried

explanation.surface: A slim machine that is light enough to take with you.
explanation.definitionFit: A compact portable PC is one used on the knees; as an adjective the word means portable.

clue.text: Called for someone with skill to reverse adverse economic situation

indicators.note: to reverse means the joined words for called and skill are read backwards

parts.note: paged means called for over a public address
art means skill, craft

explanation.surface: A skilled worker is summoned to turn round a poor economy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to reverse' turns PAGEDART round; 'someone with' only joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade gap is a deficit when a country imports more than it exports.

clue.text: Explain why, as reported in this magazine

indicators.note: as reported means the words for explain and why are heard spoken

parts.note: to gloss is to explain a text, and the word why is said like the letter Y

explanation.surface: Asks for reasons, as stated in this periodical.
explanation.definitionFit: A glossy is a magazine printed on shiny paper.

clue.text: Novel to read in equally divided parts

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters of the words to read in are made into something new

explanation.surface: A book that is to be read in installments of equal size.
explanation.definitionFit: Rationed means shared out in fixed allowances, portioned evenly.

clue.text: General writing on and off, for example?

parts.note: Mark Antony was a Roman general
MS is a manuscript, a piece of writing

explanation.surface: A military commander writes intermittently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on and off' looks like 'intermittently', but the words on and off are a pair of opposites.
explanation.definitionFit: Words with opposite meanings, like the pair given, are called opposites by grammarians.

clue.text: Runs round to gallery to copy Turner

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
O is round in shape
the Tate is a London art gallery

explanation.surface: An artist hurries round to the Tate to make copies of Turner's paintings.
explanation.walkthrough: J. M. W. Turner's paintings hang in the Tate; but the definition reads Turner as one who turns, so to copy him is to spin.
explanation.definitionFit: To revolve is to imitate anything that turns.
